It uses pure digital logic and finite state machines instead of arithmetic multipliers, making it suitable for ultra-low-power Edge AI. The design includes 32 Tsetlin Automata, each implemented as a 4-bit saturating up/down counter. It is optimized for low-power operation and targets edge AI applications.
results.summary: This project implements a scanline triangle rasterizer that outputs VGA video at 640x480 resolution with 2 bits per color. It uses a single combined multiply-and-divide unit to calculate triangle edges, updating state during H-blank periods. The design can be configured via SPI-like UIO pins to change the rendered geometry and color. It requires a TinyVGA PMOD adapter and optionally an MCU for configuration.

results.summary: This project is a 16-bit computer based on the Nand2Tetris Hack architecture, with a CPU that fetches instructions via SPI from an off-chip memory module. The memory module, simulated on an RP2040, stores both ROM and RAM partitions. The design provides general-purpose I/O and is intended to run programs loaded into the RP2040's ROM section. It is a working implementation of the Hack computer with modifications for physical feasibility.
